name: Nails
label: Southern Lord
lede: Todd Jones spent years in other people's hardcore bands, then started one where most songs run under two minutes. Kurt Ballou has recorded all four albums.

eras.title: A lifer with a Minor Threat CD
eras.text: Todd Jones grows up in Oxnard's hardcore scene, plays in a string of small bands, then spends years as the guitarist in other people's, Terror among them. Nails is what he starts when he's done waiting for a band that sounds like the one he wants to hear.

years.h: Todd Jones plays his first show in Oxnard with It Doesn't Matter
years.p: He puts it around New Year's 1995 or 1996 and says he played bass. The band is on the 1996 compilation Localism; Betrayed, Internal Affairs and FireBurn follow.
years.xp:
A friend's borrowed Minor Threat CD hit him at about 13 or 14. "I've been waiting my whole life to hear this," he told No Echo, and called it one of the most profound experiences he's had.

Next came the Revelation-inspired straight-edge band Carry On. "They were my favorite band at that time, and so I joined," he said. After that, [[Terror|697eba1a-bf52-46b1-a19f-4d7190b63e5c]] and Scott Vogel.

years.p: Carry On is over, and Jones takes the guitar spot in Terror, the Los Angeles band rooted in New York hardcore. The job makes his name, and it is where Nails starts.
years.xp: Jones told No Echo that he and Vogel sat down to settle a style. "We decided it was gonna be NYHC," he said.

eras.title: Two minutes, no filler
eras.text: Nails start in December 2007 with Jones, drummer Taylor Young and bassist John Gianelli. Within two years they're recording short, brutal songs at Kurt Ballou's studio in Salem, Massachusetts.

years.src: Southern Lord: Nails · No Echo · Wikipedia: Nails
years.h: Jones starts Nails in December 2007 so nobody else picks the style
years.p: Southern Lord dates the band to that month: Jones, drummer [[Taylor Young|b819904a-345d-4cc9-95b9-ee0bf9b3c3d2]] and bassist John Gianelli. Jones had been out of bands for a while and wanted to stop negotiating a sound with other people.
years.xp:
"I wanted to start Nails to do what I wanted to do," Jones told No Echo, rather than join two or three other people and work out a style. Of the result he says: "Everything about it is blunt, mean, and aggressive."

His own taste ran to crust, death metal and Japanese hardcore, with Agnostic Front, Discharge, Slayer and Sheer Terror among the names he cites. Southern Lord later described the sound as the good AmRep bands of the nineties plus Age of Quarrel-era Cro-Mags riffs at breakneck speed.

years.h: The first Nails record is a 12-inch, Obscene Humanity
years.p: It introduces the sound before any full-length. The 2020 reissue of Unsilent Death later added three of its tracks.

years.src: Wikipedia: Unsilent Death · Southern Lord: Nails
years.p: Recorded December 27, 2009 to January 2, 2010 with Kurt Ballou at God City in Salem. Six Feet Under put out the CD, and Jones pressed the vinyl himself on his Streetcleaner label.
years.xp:
Wikipedia gives the release as March 12, 2010 and the running time as 13 minutes 52 seconds. Ballou engineered and mixed it, the start of a working relationship that has covered every Nails album since.

Southern Lord later reissued it, including a 10th anniversary edition. The clip above is a full set filmed that August.

years.big: "He knows how to record an HM2 pedal."
years.h: Kurt Ballou, a friend since 2001, records every Nails album
years.p: Jones told Heavy Blog Is Heavy why Ballou gets the job. The HM2 is the buzzsaw guitar distortion behind the Nails tone.
years.xp: Jones says he has known Ballou since 2001. "He's like my friend, I'll text him and he'll actually text me back," he said.

eras.title: Southern Lord takes them on
eras.text: Nails move to a label that knows heavy music, and by the time Abandon All Life arrives the band is no longer an underground rumor.

years.cap: Nails' drummer at PhilaMOCA, Philadelphia, August 11, 2012
years.h: Nails split a 7-inch with Skin Like Iron
years.p: The split comes out in 2012, and Obscene Humanity gets its own 7-inch pressing the same year.

years.cap: Nails at Broad Street Ministry, Philadelphia, May 4, 2013
years.src: Wikipedia: Abandon All Life · Heavy Blog Is Heavy
years.p: Released March 28, 2013 on Southern Lord, recorded over New Year at God City with Kurt Ballou. The longest song, Suum Cuique, runs past five minutes; the whole record runs 17 minutes 14 seconds.
years.xp:
Recording ran December 27, 2012 to January 2, 2013. Brad Boatright mastered it and Andy Saba played session lead guitar. Metacritic lists 80/100.

Jones is harder on it than the critics. He told Heavy Blog Is Heavy it was "really aggressive" but not hook-oriented: "you feel like you got beat up, but you don't really remember much of the beating."

years.cap: Nails at With Full Force, Roitzschjora, Germany
years.h: Jones tours four to six weeks a year and keeps the office job
years.p: He works in an office and keeps Nails away from his coworkers. The limit is deliberate: he says he'd rather protect the other things in his life than tour full time.
years.xp:
"We only tour about a month. Four to six weeks out of the year," Jones told CVLT Nation. Of the office: "I work in an office with a bunch of suit and ties and, you know, they're pretty reserved people. I kinda keep what I do away from them."

He doesn't dress the part either: "I've never had a Mohawk, I don't need to go in public and dress like an extreme person."

eras.title: Billboard 200, then a cancelled tour
eras.text: Jones wanted the extremity of Abandon All Life with the catchiness and thickness of Unsilent Death. It becomes Nails' biggest release, then a European tour disappears and promoters announce a hiatus.

years.cap: Nails in a press photo, c. 2016: Todd Jones, Taylor Young and John Gianelli
years.src: Wikipedia: You Will Never Be One of Us · Heavy Blog Is Heavy
years.h: Nails reach number 127 on the Billboard 200
years.p: You Will Never Be One of Us came out June 17, 2016 on Nuclear Blast. It runs 21 minutes 43 seconds and includes the eight-minute-plus They Come Crawling Back.
years.xp:
Recorded December 27, 2015 to January 6, 2016 with Kurt Ballou at God City. LA Weekly ranked it number one among its top metal albums of 2016, and it appeared on year-end lists in Rolling Stone, Metal Hammer and Metal Injection.

Jones described the plan to Heavy Blog Is Heavy as taking the extremity of Abandon All Life and the catchiness and thickness of Unsilent Death and combining them. "In my opinion we accomplished it," he said.
play: You Will Never Be One of Us

years.cap: Todd Jones at Webster Hall, New York, June 22, 2016
years.h: Nails cancel a European tour, and promoters announce a hiatus
years.p: On July 25, 2016 the promoters said the band had no plans to play live or record again. Jones said Nails had never taken a hiatus.
years.xp:
The cancellation also removed a spot on the Ozzfest Meets Knotfest bill. Nails were back on stage that December at The Power of the Riff festival, and they released a split 7-inch with Full of Hell the same year.

None of the sources give a reason for the cancellation.

eras.title: A Cavalera guest spot, then two exits
eras.text: Nails put out less and play less. In 2019 Max Cavalera guests on a 7-inch, and in spring 2020 Young and Gianelli, the other two founders, leave a day apart.

years.h: Max Cavalera guests on the I Don't Want to Know You 7-inch
years.p: The Sepultura and Soulfly founder joins Nails on the 2019 release.

years.h: Drummer Taylor Young quits, and bassist John Gianelli follows a day later
years.p: Young announced his exit in early spring 2020 and Gianelli confirmed his the next day, leaving Todd Jones as the only original member.

years.h: Unsilent Death turns 10 with a Southern Lord reissue
years.p: Released November 27, 2020, it adds three Obscene Humanity songs and two previously unreleased songs from the original sessions.

eras.title: Same name, new band
eras.text: After nearly three years of silence and eight years since the last album, Jones builds a new Nails lineup and goes back to Kurt Ballou.

years.big: "I didn't want Nails to come back like a reunion band."
years.h: Nails announce a new album on Instagram, with Ballou at the board
years.p: Jones told No Echo he wanted to come back with new material. The November 2023 post confirmed a Nuclear Blast release, recorded at God City.
years.xp:
The drummer search was narrow, Jones told No Echo: "I need someone who can play double bass. But I also need that drummer to be able to play punk rock-type beats."

"I play in bands to make music," he said.

years.cap: Nails in a press photo, c. 2024: Jones with Shelby Lermo, Carlos Cruz and Andrew Solis
years.src: Wikipedia: Every Bridge Burning · No Echo
years.h: Eight years on, Every Bridge Burning runs 17 minutes 47 seconds
years.p: Out August 30, 2024 with guitarist Shelby Lermo, drummer Carlos Cruz and bassist Andrew Solis. The singles were Imposing Will, Give Me the Painkiller and Lacking the Ability to Process Empathy.
years.xp:
Recorded October 2023 to January 2024. Jones says the record is about isolation and deteriorating friendships, and that a lot of it came out after Covid.

Lermo was in Ulthar, Cruz plays in Warbringer, and Solis in Despise You and Apparition.

years.h: A Fear Based Life 7-inch is listed for 2026
years.p: Wikipedia lists the 7-inch under 2026 and gives no month or label.
